note: Style contract for the D3 raider steed's charge warning lane. There is deliberately NO PNG in this file: where the danger is and which way it points come only from Core, through the shared world projection Unity already uses for actors. The art never decides the edge.

core.owner: Core (single writer). Rules quoted from docs/harness/r04-implementation-01.md and docs/genesis-balance.md D3 as technical tuning, not balance-final
core.rule: warning 1.2 s while D3 stands still; the target is the player position locked at warning start; then a 0.6 s straight dash at speed ratio 1.30 along the locked direction; 6 s reuse from the dash end; overlapping target uses Core's stable fixed direction; arena bounds and contact damage / invulnerability follow the existing Core rules; no extra dash damage
core.projectionNeeded: for drawing, Unity reads from Core: the dash start point (D3 position at warning start), the dash end point Core will actually reach (after any arena clamp), and the contact half-width Core uses for the D3 contact test. Unity must not recompute these from art numbers

nominalForBoardsOnly.read: BattleTuning defaults in src/BibleSurvivor.Core/BattleWorld.cs at the start of this task (read-only): PlayerSpeed 3 wu/s, PlayerRadius 0.25 wu, EnemyRadius 0.2 wu
nominalForBoardsOnly.dashLengthWhy: 1.30 x 3 wu/s x 0.6 s, before any arena clamp
nominalForBoardsOnly.halfWidthWhy: PlayerRadius + EnemyRadius, the contact distance in the current Core contact test

sourcePx.meaning: world units x PPU 32 at SOURCE asset density, for the review board only; not Unity screen pixels

nominalForBoardsOnly.warning: if Core changes any of these, the runtime lane follows Core; nothing here is re-tuned by hand

placement.shape: capsule (stadium): the set of points within halfWidth of the segment start -> end. It is the area where the player's centre would meet D3's contact test during the dash
placement.boundary: the OUTER edge of the black line is the danger boundary. Nothing is drawn outside it, so the picture never makes the danger look larger than Core's
placement.direction: two chevrons inside the capsule on the centre line, pointing from start to end, at 45% and 75% of the segment; each chevron stays inside the capsule (arm reach <= halfWidth - 2 line widths)
mustNot: use a sprite or texture whose drawn edge decides the hit area
fit the lane into the 32 px actor cell
add a fill or glow outside the boundary
re-aim, extend or shorten the lane during the warning (the target is locked)

style.reuse: same line style as the R03 slam warning (art-genesis-r03 src/telegraph_r03.json): black outer + white inner

lines.name: inner
lines.from: 2 source px inside the boundary, inward

lines.name: chevrons
lines.colour: white.0 with a 1 source px outline.0 edge

style.widthRule: widths scale with the actor pixel scale (source px x scale) and never drop below 1 screen px each
style.fill: none. The ground stays visible inside the lane
style.timing: appears at warning start, static for the whole 1.2 s (no blinking, pulsing or full-screen flash), removed when the dash starts. Progress is shown by the D3 pose (windup frames 0 -> 1 at 0.6 s), not by the lane
style.lowFx: always shown: the lane is gameplay information, not an optional effect; same in low-effects, muted and small-window modes
style.readability: black outer + white inner reads on dark grass, the light path and in greyscale
